PAKISTAN COTTON CESS RULES, 2012
PAKISTAN COTTON CESS RULES, 2012
[Gazette of Pakistan, Extraordinary, Part II,
29th March, 2012]
S.R.O. 307(I)/2012,
dated 27-3-2012.---In exercise of the powers conferred by section 15 of the
Cotton Cess Act, 1923 (XIV of 1923) the Federal Government is pleased to make
the following rules, namely:---
1. Short title and
commencement.---(1) These rules
may be called the Pakistan Cotton Cess Rules, 2012.
(2) They shall come into
force at once.
2. Definition.---In these rules, unless the context otherwise
requires,---
(a) "Act" means the
Cotton Cess Act, 1923 (XIV of 1923); and
(b) "Organization"
means the head quarters of the Committee, its research institutes and station
or sub-stations.
3. Appointment and term of
members.---(1) The Federal
Government shall appoint members of the Committee by notification in the
official Gazette.
(2) The Federal Government
may, however, terminate the membership of a member before completion of his
term in the public interest.
(3) If a vacancy in the
constitution of the Committee occurs by death, resignation or otherwise, of an
ex-officio member another member shall be appointed in his place who shall hold
office for the unexpired period of the term of his predecessor.
(4) The term of the member of
the Committee, other than ex-officio member shall be three years.
4. Minimum number of
meetings.---The Committee shall
hold at least two meetings in a year.
(2) The quorum for meeting of
the committee shall be at least sixty per cent of the total membership.
5. Records of business.---The committee shall maintain complete record of
business of the committee including the confidential reports, minutes of
meeting of the committee and sub-committees and transaction of business. The
copies of the same shall be forwarded to the Federal Government and all members
of the committee.
6. Power of the Committee to
contract.---(1) The Committee has
the power to enter into contract:
Provided that every
contract which extends beyond a period of three years, or involves expenditure
in excess of rupees one million shall require prior sanction of the Federal
Government.
(2) The Committee may,
subject to sub-rule (1) by resolution, delegate to Vice-President or Chief
Executive Officer (CEO) such powers of entry into contract on its behalf as it
deems appropriate and to the extent specified in the resolution.
(3) Contracts shall not be
binding on the Committee unless they are executed by the Vice-President or CEO
and are authenticated by the common seal of the Committee.
7. Power of the Committee
for appointment etc.---The
Committee shall submit its recommendations to the Federal Government for
creation of new posts. The Committee shall also specify and recommend the
remuneration, terms of appointment, age, qualification, experience, job
description etc., for these posts.
8. Appointment, functions
and powers of CEO.---(1) The
Federal Government shall appoint the Chief Executive Officer (CEO) for a period
of three years, extendable by another period of three years, on basis of their
performance.
(2) The CEO shall be
responsible for efficient and effective administration and management of the
organization. The Federal Government may delegate powers to CEO to appoint,
promote, dismiss the officers and officials, on the recommendation of
departmental selection committee or departmental promotion committee, as the
case may be.
9. Appointment, Functions
and powers of Chief Financial Officer.---(1) The Federal Government shall appoint Chief Financial Officer (CFO)
for a period of three years, extendable by another period of three years, on
basis of his performance.
(2) The CFO shall be
responsible for all financial matters, including expenditures, income,
investments, cess collection etc. He shall formulate a financial policy within
three months of his appointment and submit for approval of the Federal
Government. He shall also be responsible for making annual budget estimates,
